name: Tenofovir alafenamide
drug_class: Nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NtRTI; phosphonamidate prodrug of tenofovir)
route_note: oral tablet once daily, alone for hepatitis B or in HIV fixed-dose combinations

discovery.note: Phosphonamidate prodrug designed to stay stable in plasma and release tenofovir inside lymphocytes and hepatocytes, mainly via cathepsin A.

tagline: Newer tenofovir prodrug: a fraction of the dose, gentler on kidneys and bone
summary: Tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) is a prodrug of tenofovir that is more stable in plasma than tenofovir disoproxil and is converted to the active drug mainly inside cells. This gives high intracellular levels with about 90% lower plasma tenofovir, reducing effects on kidneys and bone. It is used in HIV combinations, for HIV PrEP and for chronic hepatitis B.
mechanism: TAF enters lymphocytes, macrophages and hepatocytes (via OATP1B1/1B3 uptake in the liver) and is hydrolysed by cathepsin A, and in the liver by carboxylesterase 1, to tenofovir. Cellular kinases then form tenofovir diphosphate.
Tenofovir diphosphate inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and HBV polymerase as a chain terminator, exactly as with tenofovir disoproxil; the difference lies in where the active drug is generated.
uses: HIV-1 infection, as part of combination tablets (Genvoya, Descovy, Odefsey, Biktarvy, Symtuza)
HIV-1 pre-exposure prophylaxis with emtricitabine (Descovy; not for receptive vaginal sex in the US label)
Chronic hepatitis B with compensated liver disease (Vemlidy)

history.title: First approval
history.detail: TAF is first approved in the four-drug single tablet Genvoya in November 2015.

history.title: Descovy and Vemlidy
history.detail: Emtricitabine/TAF (Descovy) is approved for HIV, and TAF alone (Vemlidy) for chronic hepatitis B.

history.title: Biktarvy
history.detail: Bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF is approved and becomes the most prescribed HIV regimen in the US.

history.title: PrEP
history.detail: Descovy is approved for PrEP after the DISCOVER trial in men who have sex with men and transgender women.

history.title: HBV in adolescents
history.detail: Vemlidy is approved in the US for adolescents with chronic hepatitis B, later extended to younger children.

pk.half_life: plasma TAF about 0.5 h; intracellular tenofovir diphosphate very long
pk.bioavailability: not established; high-fat meal increases exposure
pk.metabolism: cathepsin A (lymphocytes) and carboxylesterase 1 (hepatocytes) to tenofovir; weak CYP3A substrate
pk.excretion: mainly as tenofovir in urine and faeces

serious: new-onset or worsening renal impairment (less frequent than with tenofovir disoproxil)
weight gain and lipid increases compared with TDF
safety.boxed_warning: Severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B in patients co-infected with HBV who discontinue the drug (US label).

facts: The daily dose of TAF (10–25 mg) is about a tenth of the 300 mg dose of tenofovir disoproxil.
Generic versions are made in India under Gilead's voluntary licences for low- and middle-income countries, while patents remain in the US and Europe.
